answer: A rack of forged lookout tags booked every 12-minute flare window on Corbel stair. To claim a slot, a ranger hikes 1.1 km up the shale switchback, parks a 70 g serialized brass ring in the raven loft at hut 4 for 14 minutes until a 3 mm soot band forms on the inner rim, then carries the still-warm ring 80 m to the west ridge cairn and photographs it beside tagged post 9 and the 05:31 beacon log. A second walker must match soot thickness within 12%. If the ring cools clean, post 9's notch is missing, or clocks differ over 80 seconds, the bond burns and that tag is frozen 11 days.
